name: Laser-based 3-D Volumetric Display (Rotating Helix with AO Scanner)
aliases: Laser-based rotating double helix volumetric display
definition: A hardware display technique that projects a laser beam onto a rotating reflective double helix to form discrete 3D volume points (voxels). The x-y coordinates of each voxel are determined by the laser beam's position via an Acousto-Optic (AO) scanner, while the z coordinate is determined by the physical height of the point on the helical surface. Light scatters from the helix surface, making voxels appear to emanate from specific points in real space for naked-eye viewing.
